question: Can the existing two-person anonymous-potential cycle proof supply explicit nonnegative rational flow coefficients for the full K-projected independent-background method?
model: Finite nonempty common label set L, n=2, any complete ordered formal strategy sigma. Write A=sigma(empty), beta(a)=sigma(a). No count-policy assumption, positivity, DR, self-crowding, or client representation is needed for the coordinate construction. To infer a numerical inequality, the actual IC arcs must be nonnegative and f must be a common deletion marginal. CAG is one such case and W then equals coverage.
quantifiers: For every such sigma and every rational query pi in Delta(L), construct nonnegative rational lambda and a query-independent rational background Qbar with full K(d-div(lambda)-2 sum_b Qbar(b)s_b(pi))=0. The same Qbar works for every pi; lambda depends on pi. This is n=2 only, not universal H_root for all n.

definitions.demand: d=delta_(q*,A)+delta_(q*,beta(A)); if A=beta(A), this is twice the same coordinate, exactly as occupancy demand requires.
definitions.projection: K delta_(q,a)=epsilon_q-epsilon_(q-e_a), retaining all size-2 and size-1 potential coordinates.
definitions.cycle: Choose any directed cycle of the finite function beta. Let rho be uniform on that cycle and zero elsewhere; beta_*rho=rho.
definitions.background: Qbar(e_a)=(rho_a+1[a=A])/2. It has nonnegative rational mass summing to one and does not observe the realized query.

flows.actual_origin: Root IC comparing prescribed A with forced a followed by the same beta.
Last-player IC at the actual ordered history (a), comparing prescribed beta(a) with b.
An additional copy of the same legitimate last-player comparison at the actual root history A.
flows.mass: pi_b, added to any mass from the previous row

coordinate_proof: Every coefficient is nonnegative rational. Repeated arcs receive summed masses. A coincident tail/head is zero and may be omitted; no unavailable comparison is created.
With head-minus-tail divergence, the R arcs contribute delta_(q*,A)-sum_a rho_a delta_(q_a,a).
The rho*pi last-player arcs contribute sum_a rho_a delta_(q_a,beta(a))-sum_(a,b)rho_a*pi_b delta_(e_a+e_b,b).
The additional actual-history last-player arcs contribute delta_(q*,beta(A))-sum_b pi_b delta_(e_A+e_b,b).
Therefore div(lambda)=d+C-2 sum_c Qbar(c)s_c(pi), where C=sum_a rho_a[delta_(q_a,beta(a))-delta_(q_a,a)].
Full K sends C to sum_a rho_a[epsilon_(e_beta(a))-epsilon_(e_a)], which is zero by beta_*rho=rho. Size-2 coordinates cancel within each summand, and all size-1 coordinates cancel by stationarity.
Thus d-div(lambda)-2 sum_c Qbar(c)s_c(pi)=-C has exactly zero full K projection. No LP solve, sampled identities, omitted potential layer, or arbitrary extra arc is used.
actual_new_guarantee: The two-person branch has an explicit certificate inside the exact IC-only subgraph, hence also inside IC union the permitted universal same-label arcs by assigning zero to the latter. For any common deletion-potential table satisfying those ICs, W>=2 E_(pi,Qbar)f. For rational CAG payoffs choose a rational optimal query to obtain W>=2v_2. The numerical two-person guarantee and cycle background were already proved in the source; the new content to deduplicate is this explicit lambda/full-K input certificate.
scope_boundaries: C need not vanish in ordinary payoff coordinates for a cycle of length at least three. The claim is full K-projected conservation, not ordinary graph conservation.
Only n=2 is covered. Higher-person H_root existence, all-background aggregate safety, and the general half problem remain separate.
The arbitrary formal-strategy coordinate identity does not certify that an arbitrary strategy is a CAG SPE. Nonnegative ICs and a shared deletion potential are required for the numerical consequence.
Rational query pi gives rational flows; general real anonymous payoffs need not have a rational optimal query. CAG payoffs are rational, so the rational-optimum application is valid there.

The construction uses at most O(|L|^2) explicit arc entries and a cycle of length at most |L|. It is a given-query certificate construction, not a claim about solving the higher-person optimization problem.
